JSON: Name: region_aware_spatial_robustness_benchmark Title: Region-aware multi-attack benchmarking of spatial robustness for semantic segmentation under localized natural and adversarial corruptions Short Hypothesis: A region-aware multi-attack adversarial analysis produces a systematically larger degradation in non-corrupted-region accuracy (higher relative corruption error) than single localized attacks across state-of-the-art semantic segmentation models. Related Work: Existing robustness evaluations emphasize either whole-image natural corruptions or adversarial attacks but rarely both in a spatially localized manner. Benchmarks derived from image-level corruptions evaluate average model resilience to weather and noise but do not measure how localized faults spread across non-perturbed image regions. Prior adversarial-patch and localized-attack work demonstrates model vulnerabilities but typically uses single-attack formulations, physical-patch scenarios, or untargeted single-run attacks; these approaches do not account for multi-objective optimization across many pixels and therefore under-estimate worst-case spatial vulnerability. Comparative studies between convolutional and transformer-based segmentation models highlight differing global robustness trends, yet they do not quantify spatial effects inside and outside corrupted regions. Common metrics (mIoU, pixel accuracy) lack region-aware decompositions, and there is no standard procedure to iteratively expand adversarial coverage to reveal pixels left unchallenged by single attacks. Abstract: We present a region-aware evaluation framework for benchmarking spatial robustness of semantic segmentation models under localized natural and adversarial corruptions. The approach defines region-specific metrics that separate accuracy inside corrupted regions from accuracy in non-corrupted regions and introduces a region-aware multi-attack adversarial procedure that iteratively refines fooling regions to expose additional vulnerable pixels. The primary contributions are: (1) formal region-aware metrics for localized robustness; (2) an algorithm that composes multiple localized adversarial runs to approximate worst-case spatial effects; and (3) an empirical benchmark comparing convolutional and transformer-based segmentation models and testing weighted ensemble trade-offs between natural and adversarial localized robustness. Expected outcomes include demonstrable differences in how architectures propagate localized corruption, identification of pixels overlooked by single attacks, and evidence that simple model ensembles can produce measurable trade-offs between robustness to natural localized corruptions and worst-case adversarial perturbations. Experiments: Datasets: Cityscapes validation set (500 images) at original resolution; additional synthetic localized corruptions generated from noise/blur/brightness/snow transformations with severity levels {1,3,5}. Models: SegFormer (b0,b1), BiSeNet (X39,R18,R101), DeepLabv3 (ResNet, MobileNet), PSPNet, ICNet, DDRNet23, DDRNet23Slim, PIDNet (s,m,l). Baselines: (A) Clean evaluation; (B) single localized adversarial attack (iterative l_infty PGD-style localized patch) with N=1; (C) image-level adversarial attack (global PGD) as reference. Proposed: region-aware multi-attack adversarial analysis (Algorithm with parameters N in {1,3,5}, iterations per attack in {50,100,200}, patch size in {100x100,200x200}, eps in {16/255,32/255}, patch positions center and corner). Natural localized baseline: randomized localized application of ImageNet-C style transforms with patch ratio r in {0.3,0.5}. Metrics: pixel-wise accuracy inside corrupted region A_M, pixel-wise accuracy outside corrupted region A_nonM, relative corruption error RCE = (A_nonM_clean - A_nonM_corrupted)/A_nonM_clean, corrupted-region error CE, mIoU, cumulative attacked-pixel coverage (fraction of ground-truth pixels misclassified by any attack run). Protocol: all attacks are white-box; run 5 random seeds per configuration; report mean±std. Ablations: (1) vary N to quantify incremental coverage and RCE; (2) vary iterations per attack to measure convergence; (3) compare patch positions; (4) weighted ensemble fusion of one model robust to natural corruptions and one robust to adversarial corruptions, sweep gamma in [0,1] and report RCE_natural and RCE_adversarial and clean accuracy; (5) assess sensitivity to corruption severity levels. Hardware/compute: single-GPU per run, batch size 1, deterministic preprocessing, gradient steps per iteration matching attack iterations. Risk Factors and Limitations: High computational cost: multi-attack iterative adversarial analysis at high-resolution images requires substantial GPU time and memory; scaling to larger datasets will be expensive. White-box requirement: gradient-based multi-attack evaluation assumes access to model internals; black-box or physical attacks may behave differently. Synthetic natural corruptions and static patch placements may not capture full physical-world variability and could bias conclusions. Metric limitations: pixel-wise accuracy and RCE focus on per-pixel degradation and may not reflect downstream task safety or perceptual significance; mIoU averaging can obscure spatially localized failures. Generalization: results on Cityscapes and selected architectures may not generalize to other domains, sensor modalities, or architectures with different attention mechanisms. Ensemble trade-offs: weighted softmax fusion may overfit validation conditions and cause unexpected drops on out-of-distribution inputs. Adversarial arms race: methods that reveal worst-case vulnerabilities can prompt countermeasures that shift failure modes, limiting long-term guarantees.
